about: Proposed region definitions for a detailed map of the United Arab Emirates: all seven emirates, proposed as one region for the whole country, with a box for each emirate so that seven separate maps remain possible. A proposal for discussion (docs/REGIONS-AE.md); no code reads this file, and it does not ship. Sources are national or global, so they are listed once under country_layers, and each region points there.

codes.proposal: AE for the whole country; ISO 3166-2:AE codes AE-AZ, AE-AJ, AE-DU, AE-FU, AE-RK, AE-SH, AE-UQ for the seven emirates.
codes.why: AE is not in STATE_CODES (engine/address_search.py) or NAMES (packaging/state_maps.py). The part after the hyphen is not safe alone: AZ already means Arizona.
codes.verified: Read from Wikipedia's copy of the ISO list and from the shapeISO field of geoBoundaries' emirate file, which carries all seven. The ISO site itself was not checked.

addressing.levels: Emirate; city; community, district or area; street; building or villa. In practice a P.O. Box as well.
addressing.order: Postal: name, P.O. Box number, emirate or city, country ("PO BOX 111 / DUBAI / UNITED ARAB EMIRATES"). Abu Dhabi's Onwani: building number, street name, city ("26, Al Seray Street, Khalifa City, Abu Dhabi", from a news report).

postal_code.format: None on the Universal Postal Union's sheet: deliveries are made to P.O. Boxes only. News reports say Onwani gives Abu Dhabi locations a postal code; its format was not found.

source.dataset: Addressing sheet for the United Arab Emirates (09/2014)

geographic_codes.makani: Ten digits, written as two groups of five ("30032 95320"), one per building entrance; by a trade press report five digits are an easting and five a northing. Official in Dubai, Ajman, Umm Al Quwain, Fujairah and Ras Al Khaimah by the app's own description. The grid behind the number was not found.

addressing.notes: Addresses are written in Arabic or in Latin letters, and Latin spellings vary (Abū Z̧aby and Abu Dhabi, Ash Shāriqah and Sharjah). normalize() in engine/address_search.py keeps only a-z and 0-9, so Arabic script is dropped and "Ra's al Khaymah" becomes "ra s al khaymah". is_address_query() needs a number and then a space, so "26 Al Seray Street" is an address query and "26, Al Seray Street" is not; it reads "30032 95320" as house number 30032, and _parts() then takes 95320 as a five-digit postcode, leaving no street. tools/build_addresses.py keeps only country = 'US'. Checked in this repository on 2026-11-17.

bbox_source.method: Extent of every vertex of the emirate's polygons in the full-resolution GeoJSON (7 features, 2,254,355 bytes; source data of 19 January 2023, built 12 December 2023); margin is 0.15 degrees, rounded outward to 0.01.
bbox_source.cross_check: Natural Earth 1:10m countries gives 51.5693, 22.6209, 56.3836, 26.0748 for the UAE; the two agree to 0.04 degrees on the west edge and 0.011 on the others.

grouped.name: Dubai and the Northern Emirates
grouped.note: An alternative if one map for the country is too large: Abu Dhabi alone, and these six together. No ISO code exists for the group.

boundary_notes: Ajman, Dubai, Fujairah, Ras Al Khaimah and Sharjah each have two or more separate pieces of at least 10 km2 in this file (Ajman three, Fujairah three, Sharjah four); Dubai's second piece lies about 34 km east of its main one.
With the margin, each emirate's box reaches into all six others.
No polygon in this file covers Abu Musa or the Greater and Lesser Tunbs (tested at 55.03 E 25.875 N, 55.305 E 26.26 N and 55.145 E 26.24 N; the positions are from general knowledge).
The country box also holds parts of Oman and Saudi Arabia, as any box holds its neighbours.
